svg.title: Antiarrhythmic drugs: stable patients get drugs, unstable get electricity, arrested get CPR, electricity and drugs; after treating precipitants, AV-nodal drugs (beta blocker, calcium channel blocker, digoxin, adenosine) serve supraventricular rhythms and channel blockers (class I procainamide and lidocaine, class III amiodarone and sotalol) reach ventricular ones; each drug's use and what rules it out, plus torsades de pointes caused by QT-prolonging drugs

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: Arrhythmia: STABLE → drugs · UNSTABLE → electricity · DEAD → CPR + electricity + drugs

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: FIRST treat precipitants: low K+, Mg2+, phosphate · ischemia · hypoxemia · catecholamines · QT-prolonging drugs

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: sinus tachycardia: treat the CAUSE (bleeding → fluids, blood), never slow it · every antiarrhythmic can CAUSE arrhythmia

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: arrest: CPR, shock ventricular fibrillation (VF) or pulseless ventricular tachycardia (VT), epinephrine every 3–5 min,

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: then amiodarone or lidocaine if it persists

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: Slow the ATRIOVENTRICULAR (AV) NODE: SUPRAVENTRICULAR rhythms

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: the ventricular rate falls; a ventricular rhythm is untouched

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: Block Na+ or K+ channels: VENTRICULAR too
